title: Director, Application & AI Security
description: About Lantern Lantern is the specialty care platform connecting people with the best care when they need it most. By curating a Network of Excellence comprised of the nation's top specialists for surgery, cancer care, infusions and more, Lantern delivers excellent care with significant cost savings to employers and their workforces. Lantern also pairs members with a dedicated care team, including Care Advocates and nurses, for the entirety of their care journey, helping them get back to good health, back to their families and back to work. With convenient access to specialists nationwide, Lantern means quality care is within driving distance for most. Lantern is trusted by the nation's largest employers to deliver care to more than 6 million members across the country. Learn more about us at lanterncare.com. Lantern is the specialty care platform, connecting people with high-quality, affordable specialty care close to home. We operate in a regulated healthcare environment (HIPAA, HITRUST, SOC 2), we handle protected health information at scale, and we are becoming an AI healthcare company, with AI adoption a top company priority. The Director, Application & AI Security owns application and AI security end to end: the security of the software and the AI systems Lantern builds. It is the seat most directly tied to our AI strategy. The job is to make it safe to move fast, building the golden paths and secure defaults that let teams ship product and adopt AI without waiting in a permission queue, while keeping PHI and external-model data egress genuinely protected. You will lead a growing function. At hire, the team includes a senior application security engineer, with several open roles to fill across security architecture, AI/ML security, DevSecOps, and product security. You will build that team and set the secure-design standards the whole engineering organization builds against. Our security philosophy is open by default, secure by design. Security exists to help the business move fast, safely, and the default answer is “yes, safely,” because guardrails are built into the platform, pipelines, and tooling rather than enforced by someone saying no. Gates exist only where risk genuinely warrants them, and even then they are automated, fast, and transparent. Location: Remote Responsibilities: Own application security across the development lifecycle, covering static, dynamic, and interactive analysis (SAST/DAST/SCA/IAST), code and dependency security, API security, and runtime protections such as WAF and API gateways, all delivered through engineering teams rather than filed as findings. Own AI and ML security, including model and agent security, prompt-injection and tool-use risk, and data-egress controls for third-party model providers, plus continuous AI security posture management informed by the OWASP LLM Top 10, MITRE ATLAS, and AI risk-management standards (NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001). Own security architecture and threat modeling, including secure-by-design review and ownership of cryptographic standards. Own DevSecOps and pipeline security, with scanning as a default in CI/CD and MLOps/LLMOps pipelines, release gating calibrated to risk, and software supply chain and SBOM practice. Own the security-review intake as a single front door with risk-based triage, reported against a turnaround commitment, so security accelerates the business rather than bottlenecking it. Own the application and AI security tool stack and the secure-design standards behind it. Key Deliverables in Your First Year: An AI golden path: an approved-model catalog and automated data-egress controls, so teams adopt AI on a governed route instead of case-by-case approvals. A secure SDLC paved road, with scanning in the pipeline by default and critical findings resolved within SLA. A single security-review intake that delivers fast, risk-based answers on a published turnaround. A built-out team, with the open roles filled and performing. How You Will Work: Much of this scope is delivered in partnership. Engineering carries remediation on application, API, and dependency findings. Platform Engineering operates the CI/CD pipelines you secure. AI Engineering builds the model integrations you govern on the security side, while the Governance, Risk & Compliance team owns AI use governance, meaning acceptable use, model inventory, and third-party model data-egress scoping, as the companion to your security accountability. Setting and holding clear service expectations across these partners is part of the role. Requirements: A minimum of 8 years application or product security. A minimum of 3 years leading a team with function-level accountability. Demonstrated AI and ML security ownership at production scale, including model and agent security, prompt-injection and tool-use risk, and data-egress control for third-party model providers, with working fluency in the OWASP LLM Top 10, MITRE ATLAS, and AI risk-management standards (NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001). Secure SDLC leadership across static, dynamic, and interactive analysis (SAST/DAST/SCA/IAST), dependency and software supply-chain risk, SBOM practice, and remediation delivered through engineering teams. Security architecture and threat-modeling depth, with the standing to review a design and be heard by senior engineers. DevSecOps and pipeline security experience, including scanning as a default in CI/CD, risk-calibrated release gating, and pipeline secret handling. API security experience on a platform handling regulated data. A track record of delivering security as paved roads and secure defaults rather than review gates, with evidence of adoption. Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field, or equivalent professional experience. Strong Candidates Will: Healthcare or another regulated domain where PHI or comparable data flows through AI systems. Experience standing up an AI golden path, including an approved-model catalog, a governed adoption route, and automated egress controls. Experience building a single security-review intake with risk-based triage and a turnaround commitment. Cryptographic standards ownership, including customer-managed key models. Hands-on familiarity with tools such as Snyk, GitHub Advanced Security, AI security posture management (for example, Wiz), and AI-assisted code scanning. Familiarity with AI red-teaming and adversarial-testing tooling (for example, Garak, PyRIT, Promptfoo). Product security experience shipping customer-facing security features as differentiators. Experience hiring and building a team from a single senior individual contributor. CSSLP, OSWE, GWAPT, or equivalent. Who Thrives in This Role: Guardrails over gates. You instinctively ask how to remove a queue rather than how to staff one. Engineering credibility. You earn influence with builders through technical depth, not process authority. Risk calibration. You reserve genuine gates for what earns them, namely PHI exposure, external model egress, and privileged access, and you keep even those automated and fast. Delivery orientation. You treat a roadmap as a commitment with dates. Team building. You can grow a function from one senior IC and a set of open roles. Benefits Medical Insurance Dental Insurance Vision Insurance Short & Long Term Disability Life Insurance 401k with company match Flexible Time Off Paid Parental Leave About You: You use LOGIC in your decision making and understand that progress is critical to making change. You focus on the execution of your content while balancing a fast-paced environment and you take the time to celebrate both the small & big wins. INCLUSION is a core tenant of your personal beliefs. A diverse and inclusive environment is incredibly important to you. You understand and desire to be a part of a diverse team with different experiences and perspectives & you cherish the differences in each individual that you interact with. You have the GRIT , drive and ambition to tackle big problems. Big problems require big ideas and a team that supports new ideas. You care deeply for your customers are driven to keep HUMANITY in all decisions. Your customers aren’t just the individuals using your product. They are the driving factor in your motivation to make a change. Integrity guides you in life. Focusing on the TRUTH vs. giving people the answers they want to hear. You thrive in a Team Environment. Collaboration is key in innovation and creating change. These pillars of LIGHT are a reminder to our team that we are making a difference by providing guidance and support in navigating the often complex and confusing landscape of healthcare. We hope that through this LIGHT , individuals can find their way to the best care, resources, and support they need to get back to life. If this sounds like you, we would love to connect to speak further about career opportunities at Lantern. Please apply to our role & someone from our Talent Acquisition Team will reach out to help you navigate our interview process. Lantern does not discriminate on the basis of race, sex, color, religion, age, national origin, marital status, disability, veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or any other reason prohibited by law in provision of employment opportunities and benefits.

title: Manager, CyberSecurity Risk Management
description: Headquarters: Remote About the team: The Information Security organization advances the overall state of security at Rubrik through critical initiatives and coordination of large security projects. Information Security builds technologies, tools, and processes to better enable teams at Rubrik to develop secure software and protect data and systems with appropriate security controls. Information Security also develops systems to monitor and respond to attacks against our assets, provides awareness education to teams on security best practices for data protection, and ensures data governance and data sharing relationships with third parties in order to securely protect Rubrik information. About the role: We are looking for a Manager, CyberSecurity Risk Management to join our security risk management team and support the delivery of Rubrik's cybersecurity risk management program. Working closely with the team's lead Program Manager, who owns the program, you will help drive day-to-day execution: coordinating cross-functional risk assessments, supporting risk review and acceptance processes, tracking risk remediation to closure, and producing risk reporting that gives leadership a clear view of Rubrik's cybersecurity risk posture. You will partner with Security, Engineering, Product, IT, Legal, Procurement, and Finance to keep work on track and deliver measurable outcomes. Success in this role requires strong program management discipline, solid risk and compliance knowledge, and the ability to influence and build consensus at every level of the company. What you’ll do: Support program operations for the overall Cybersecurity Risk Management Program. Support and conduct risk assessments and triage incoming security issues related to Rubrik’s core products, services, and infrastructure. Draft clear risk statements that translate technical findings into business impact, including likelihood/impact rationale and key assumptions. Maintain and update the risk register, ensuring ownership, status, target dates, and risk treatment decisions are accurate and timely. Coordinate and track cross-functional risk initiatives, managing timelines, dependencies, and action items; flag delivery risks early and drive follow-through. Drive remediation of risks to closure by conducting periodic cross-functional check-ins with risk owners to obtain updates, track milestones and target dates, document progress in the risk register, remove/escalate blockers, and communicate status through leadership reporting. Support the risk governance cadence, including preparing materials for risk committee meetings, facilitating risk acceptance and exception reviews, and tracking escalations, decisions, and actions to completion. Collect and analyze program metrics (KPIs/KRIs), build dashboards, and help prepare risk updates for leadership. Support the risk assessment program at scale, including enterprise, technical, and third-party/supplier risk assessments, helping keep methodology, quality, and turnaround times consistent. Execute and document cybersecurity risk assessments (inherent and residual) for systems, applications, cloud services, and initiatives; gather evidence and validate control implementation with stakeholders. Help map program activities to compliance obligations and frameworks (ISO 27001, SOC 2, FedRAMP, NIST CSF/800-53, PCI DSS, HIPAA) and emerging regulations (e.g., DORA, NIS2, EU AI Act). Contribute to risk quantification efforts so risks can be prioritized in business and financial terms. Support GRC tooling, automation, and AI-enabled improvement initiatives by gathering requirements, coordinating implementation tasks, piloting use cases (e.g., LLM-assisted intake triage, evidence mapping, and automated status summarization), and driving adoption of standardized workflows with appropriate governance and human review. Identify gaps and recommend process improvements to make risk management activities more efficient, consistent, and effective. Experience you'll need: 8+ years of experience in cybersecurity risk management, or GRC, including at least 3 years in a program or project management role. Experience supporting or helping scale a cybersecurity risk management program in a fast-paced technology, SaaS, or cloud company. Strong program management skills: project planning, dependency management, effort estimation, status reporting, and delivery of cross-functional initiatives. Solid working knowledge of risk management methodologies (NIST RMF / 800-37 / 800-30, ISO 27005, COBIT) and common security frameworks such as ISO 27001/2, SOC 2, FedRAMP, NIST CSF / 800-53, CIS Controls, PCI DSS, and HIPAA. Enough technical understanding of cloud, identity, network, and application security to engage credibly with engineering teams and follow remediation plans. Able to communicate risk clearly to senior stakeholders and build consensus without direct authority. Hands-on experience with agile project management and reporting tools (e.g., Jira, Confluence, Tableau). Excellent written and verbal communication, organization, and stakeholder management skills. title: Director, Finance Data, Reporting & AI
description: Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands.   About the Role Veeam’s Finance Transformation Office (FTO) is looking for a Director, Finance Data, Reporting & AI to lead how Finance uses data, reporting, analytics, and AI. This leader will own the strategy and roadmap for Veeam’s certified Finance data environment, establishing a trusted single source of truth (SSOT) that supports reporting, analytics, and AI-enabled capabilities across Finance. You will lead Finance data and reporting governance, ensuring information is accurate, well-controlled, reconciled, and ready for use in management, board, and external reporting. You’ll partner closely with Corporate Technology and Finance leaders across Controllership, FP&A, Revenue, Tax, Commercial Operations, and Treasury to deliver scalable data and reporting capabilities. You will also lead the Finance AI Engineer and help build a growing Finance data and AI team, ensuring AI solutions are grounded in certified, governed, and well-modelled data. This is a senior leadership opportunity for someone who combines strong Finance knowledge with data and AI leadership and enough technical depth to set direction, challenge solutions, and operate credibly with both technical teams and CFO-level stakeholders. What You’ll Do Set the strategy for Finance data, reporting, and AI, establishing the vision, roadmap, priorities, standards, and operating model for the function. Build and lead the Finance data and AI team, initially managing the Finance AI Engineer while hiring, coaching, and developing additional technical talent as the function grows. Own the Finance single source of truth (SSOT) and roadmap for certified datasets, semantic models, and governed data products supporting self-service analytics and reporting. Serve as Finance’s data and reporting control point, ensuring critical data is complete, accurate, reconciled to source systems, explainable, and appropriately governed before use in executive, board, or external reporting. Establish Finance data and reporting governance, including data ownership and stewardship, KPI and metric definitions, master data standards, lineage, access controls, report certification, and change management. Build scalable data-quality and reconciliation controls, including automated checks between the Finance SSOT and key systems such as NetSuite, Salesforce, and Pigment, with appropriate alerting and SOX-aware control evidence. Partner with Corporate Technology to prioritize and deliver Finance data initiatives, define requirements and data contracts, lead UAT, and establish clear ownership for solutions and ongoing operations. Lead Finance AI enablement, ensuring AI agents, natural-language interfaces, and other AI-enabled capabilities operate on certified data, governed metrics, appropriate access controls, and traceable outputs. Support financial close and executive reporting cycles, acting as a senior escalation point for data and reporting issues and helping ensure MBR, QBR, board, and other leadership reporting remains timely and trusted. Represent Finance data, reporting, and AI with senior stakeholders, communicating strategy, progress, risks, priorities, and business value to Finance and Corporate Technology leadership. What You’ll Bring 10+ years of experience in finance data, analytics engineering, business intelligence, finance systems, or a related discipline, with demonstrated ownership of enterprise data and reporting programs within a Finance organization. 3+ years of people leadership experience managing data, analytics, engineering, AI, or other technical teams, with experience setting strategy and successfully delivering AI/ML or LLM-enabled capabilities into production. Strong Finance domain expertise, including understanding of financial close, consolidation, revenue recognition, intercompany accounting, chart of accounts, and SaaS metrics such as ARR, NRR, bookings, and billings. Experience in SaaS or subscription-based businesses, with an understanding of how customer, bookings, billing, renewal, ERP, and CRM data flow into Finance reporting and analytics. Deep SQL and data-modelling expertise, including dimensional modelling and the design of curated, reusable Finance datasets and semantic layers. title: Paid Media Manager
description: Headquarters: United States How do you reach people who don't want to be marketed to? You lead with value. That's our approach with developers and the platform and security leaders who buy Coder: ads that speak to the problems they're actually solving, like where their AI agents run, who governs them, and how to keep code and data under their control. Coder is defining the AI Operating Layer , and paid media is one of the main ways we take that story to market. As our Paid Media Manager, you'll own the strategy and performance of our always-on programs across LinkedIn, Google Search, YouTube, and newer platforms like ChatGPT ads, aimed at our enterprise and target accounts. The goal is better, not just more: every dollar should reach the right people, tell the right story, and turn into pipeline. You'll direct our paid media agency and give them the Coder context they can't get on their own (ICP, positioning, target accounts, business goals). You're just as comfortable in execution as in strategy. You can audit accounts, fix what's broken, or jump in to launch campaigns, and you know what good looks like down to the platform settings. You'll report to our Demand Generation lead and work closely with product marketing, design, web, marketing ops, ABM, regional marketing, and GTM engineering. What you'll do here Own the strategy and performance of our paid channels: LinkedIn (sponsored content, document ads, thought leader ads, video and CTV), Google Search, YouTube, and ChatGPT ads. Lead our paid media agency day-to-day. Set priorities, review launches and ad copy, and hold the work to clear timelines and results. Regularly audit our ad accounts, including campaign structure, settings, audiences, conversion tracking, and spend, and jump in hands-on to build, restructure, or fix campaigns when needed. Own budget allocation, forecasting, and monthly pacing across channels and regions. Recommend where to scale, cut, or pause based on pipeline quality, not just clicks. Run a structured test-and-learn agenda across audiences, keywords and match types, offers, creative, formats, and new channels. Define the hypothesis up front and document what we learn. Build targeting around our ICP and target account lists, including retargeting, exclusion audiences, and intent signals. Tailor programs for NAMER, EMEA, and APAC and for priority verticals like financial services, partnering with regional marketing on what each market needs. Partner with PMM and design to keep ad copy and creative current with our positioning, and share back what's resonating. Work with web on landing pages and conversion paths. Own paid reporting: monthly readouts that connect spend to pipeline and revenue, with a clear point of view on what we should do next. Deliver paid air cover for launches and key moments like AWS re:Invent. What we're looking for 5–7 years of paid media or performance marketing experience, including owning multi-channel paid strategy and budgets. Deep hands-on expertise in LinkedIn Campaign Manager and Google Ads (Search and YouTube). You can build, restructure, and audit campaigns yourself, not just review an agency's work. Experience managing agencies or vendors. You hold partners accountable to results and are still someone they want to work with. A track record of owning and scaling meaningful budgets across multiple channels, including pacing, forecasting, and reallocation. Experience leading global paid programs and adjusting strategy to align with each region's priorities and performance. Comfort working with data. You can connect ad platform data with attribution and CRM tools like HockeyStack, HubSpot, or Salesforce, and turn it into decisions. A strong grasp of B2B targeting and measurement: ICP, account lists, segmentation, retargeting, exclusions, and conversion tracking. Strong project management skills across multiple campaigns, deadlines, and stakeholders, and clear communication when things shift. Curiosity about using AI tools and workflows to speed up analysis, reporting, and execution. Bonus tacos if you have Experience marketing to developers, platform engineers, or other technical buyers. Experience with ABM or intent tools such as Vector, 6sense, Common Room, or HockeyStack. Experience with emerging or programmatic channels like ChatGPT ads, CTV, StackAdapt, or Reddit. Paid experience from B2C or other industries. We value people who bring ideas from different playbooks. Our tech stack You don't need to know every tool on day one. This role works across LinkedIn Campaign Manager, Google Ads, HockeyStack, HubSpot, Salesforce, GA4, Asana, and AI tools like Claude. About Coder Coder is the leading platform for AI development Infrastructure, enabling enterprises to securely run human and AI-driven development workflows in consistent, governed environments. Coder provides self-hosted, agent-ready workspaces that unify developer productivity and platform governance. With Coder, enterprises can confidently evolve from human-only development to AI-assisted and autonomous workflows, without sacrificing security, compliance, or performance. Learn more at coder.com .
